Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{100}2^{-\left\lfloor 101k/j\right\rfloor}.
\]

For any integer \(n\ge1\),

\[
2^{-n}=\sum_{t=n+1}^{\infty}2^{-t}.
\]

Hence, interchanging the sums,

\[
S=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}2^{-t}N(t),
\]

where \(N(t)\) counts the pairs \((k,j)\) with \(k\ge1\), \(1\le j\le100\), and

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{j}\right\rfloor<t.
\]

For fixed \(j\),

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{j}\right\rfloor<t
\iff
\frac{101k}{j}<t
\iff
k<\frac{tj}{101}.
\]

The number of positive integers \(k\) satisfying this is

\[
\left\lceil \frac{tj}{101}\right\rceil-1
=
\left\lfloor\frac{tj-1}{101}\right\rfloor.
\]

Thus

\[
N(t)=\sum_{j=1}^{100}\left\lfloor\frac{tj-1}{101}\right\rfloor.
\]

Write \(t=101q+s\), where \(q\ge0\) and \(0\le s\le100\).

If \(s=0\), then

\[
N(101q)=\sum_{j=1}^{100}(qj-1)=5050q-100.
\]

If \(1\le s\le100\), since \(101\) is prime,

\[
N(101q+s)
=
\sum_{j=1}^{100}\left(qj+\left\lfloor\frac{sj}{101}\right\rfloor\right)
=
5050q+50(s-1).
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}\sum_{s=1}^{100}2^{-101q-s}\bigl(5050q+50(s-1)\bigr)
+\sum_{q=1}^{\infty}2^{-101q}(5050q-100).
\end{aligned}
\]

Let \(A=2^{-101}\). Using

\[
\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}A^q=\frac1{1-A},
\qquad
\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}qA^q=\frac{A}{(1-A)^2},
\]

and

\[
\sum_{s=1}^{100}2^{-s}=1-2^{-100},
\qquad
\sum_{s=1}^{100}(s-1)2^{-s}=1-\frac{101}{2^{100}},
\]

we get

\[
S=
\frac{5050A}{(1-A)^2}(1-2^{-100})
+
\frac{50}{1-A}\left(1-\frac{101}{2^{100}}\right)
+
\frac{5050A}{(1-A)^2}
-
\frac{100A}{1-A}.
\]

Let \(M=2^{100}\), so \(A=1/(2M)\). Simplifying,

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\frac{5050A(2-1/M)}{(1-A)^2}
+\frac{50(1-101/M)-100A}{1-A} \\
&=\frac{5050A(2-1/M)+50(1-102/M)(1-A)}{(1-A)^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(2-1/M=2(1-A)\),

\[
S=\frac{50(1-1/M)}{1-A}.
\]

Substituting \(M=2^{100}\) and \(A=2^{-101}\),

\[
S=\frac{50(1-2^{-100})}{1-2^{-101}}
=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
